evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0001, current-label alignment under the full partition is weak and modality-dependent. In CT, WSI, and WXS the mean and median silhouettes are negative and the majority of patients (73%, 78%, 47% respectively) are closer to the nearest competing set K2_C0002 than to their own set, with mean between-set distances slightly smaller than mean within-set distances. Only RNA shows a small positive mean silhouette (0.063) with a minority of negative silhouettes (29%). Thus the current membership of K2_C0001 is not consistently expressed in native patient geometry across modalities; the CT, WSI, and WXS geometries place these patients marginally closer to K2_C0002. Global geometry concordance (GRV) between modality pairs is modest (0.165-0.283) and, for CT-RNA, CT-WSI, RNA-WXS, and WSI-RNA, unlikely under exchangeable patient correspondence, but GRV describes overall patient-geometry similarity and is not itself current-boundary support. No reclustering was performed, and these alignment measurements bear on membership representation without determining accept or drop.
evidence_reports.cross_evidence_context: The prior structural-diagnostics report found both K2_C0001 and K2_C0002 screening at candidate_k=1 with a large leading eigengap, i.e., no dominant multi-cluster subdivision signal, and identified K2_C0001-K2_C0002 as the nearest candidate pair with between-set fused affinity close to within-set affinity. The present alignment evidence is consistent with that weak pair separation: in CT, WSI, and WXS the K2_C0001 samples are on average marginally closer to K2_C0002 than to their own set, while RNA shows weak positive separation. The prior report explicitly noted that no current-label alignment metric was present; this report supplies that alignment evidence.

Silhouette values are small in magnitude (absolute values below ~0.28), so separation is weak in all modalities and should not be over-interpreted.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0001, current-label alignment under the full partition is weak and modality-dependent. In CT, WSI, and WXS the mean and median silhouettes are negative and the majority of patients (73%, 78%, 47% respectively) are closer to the nearest competing set K2_C0002 than to their own set, with mean between-set distances slightly smaller than mean within-set distances. Only RNA shows a small positive mean silhouette (0.063) with a minority of negative silhouettes (29%). Thus the current membership of K2_C0001 is not consistently expressed in native patient geometry across modalities; the CT, WSI, and WXS geometries place these patients marginally closer to K2_C0002. Global geometry concordance (GRV) between modality pairs is modest (0.165-0.283) and, for CT-RNA, CT-WSI, RNA-WXS, and WSI-RNA, unlikely under exchangeable patient correspondence, but GRV describes overall patient-geometry similarity and is not itself current-boundary support. evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: For the K2_C0001-K2_C0002 pair, current-label alignment under the full partition is weak in every modality. Pair-level mean silhouettes are near zero and slightly positive (CT 0.013, RNA 0.079, WSI 0.050, WXS 0.091), with median silhouettes similarly near zero and negative fractions ranging from 26% to 46%. Mean within-set and between-set distances are close in all modalities, with between-set distances only marginally larger than within-set distances. Thus the current boundary between K2_C0001 and K2_C0002 is only weakly expressed in native patient geometry, and a substantial minority of patients in each modality are closer to the competing set than to their own set. Global geometry concordance (GRV) between modality pairs is modest (0.092-0.198) and, for CT-WSI, RNA-WXS, and WSI-RNA, unlikely under exchangeable patient correspondence, but GRV describes overall patient-geometry similarity and is not itself current-boundary support. No reclustering was performed, and these alignment measurements bear on boundary representation without determining accept, drop, split, or merge.
